newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DSF channel says unaffected by court ruling.
newsitem.headline: German DSF channel says unaffected by court ruling.

text.p: The German all-sports channel DSF, after a court ruling that said its broadcasting licence had not been issued correctly, said on Thursday the decision would have no direct impact on its ability to broadcast.

The Federal Administrative Court on Wednesday upheld a previous ruling by a Bavarian court, which in response to a complaint by Berlin media regulators agreed that errors were made in issuing DSF's original broadcasting licence.

The ruling could be a blessing in disguise, however, because as a result DSF will become one of the first German broadcasters to receive a licence based on new, more liberal broadcasting regulations that took effect in January.

Rainer Huether, DSF managing director, said he did not expect any problems in receiving a licence under the new media regulations and that the court decision would not mean the channel had to stop broadcasting.
"We are convinced that we will fulfil the new conditions without any problems," he said.
The court decision draws back to a complaint filed by Berlin media regulators against their counterparts in Bavaria, where DSF is based.
Media officials in Berlin and Brandenburg states have objected to approving DSF's licence since 1993 because of concerns that the Kirch Group, an investor in DSF, held too much broadcasting power.
Under the old rules, no company could fully own a broadcaster and there were strict limits on stake holdings.
But the new rules simply restrict market share a company can have to 30 percent. Huether said the Kirch Group falls within these parameters. DSF has market share of 1.3 percent.
Munich media mogul Leo Kirch's group has owned two thirds of DSF since it bought shares this year from publishers Axel Springer Verlag AG and Ringier-Verlag.
The remaining shares in DSF are held by Rete Invest Holding S.A., a company owned by former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi.
